newsitem.title: UK: EMAP chairman under pressure over rule change - FT.
newsitem.headline: EMAP chairman under pressure over rule change - FT.

text.p: The board of EMAP Plc is split over the future of chairman Sir John Hoskyns in a row over new procedures for removing directors, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday.

The conflict will be discussed at a meeting of the board of the magazine, radio and exhibitions group later on Tuesday, the report said. It quoted an executive director of EMAP as saying: "We could see the departure of Sir John or the calling of an extraordinary general meeting to get him out."

Several directors are concerned at Hoskyns' claim that it was EMAP's lawyers who recommended that the company's articles of association be changed at its annual meeting in July to make it easier to force directors off the board, the report said.
They think that Hoskyns and chief executive Robin Miller may have pushed for the rule change so they could force out "difficult directors."
The changes mean that directors can now be removed with the approval of 75 percent of the board. EMAP is also no longer required to have a minimum of five non-executive directors.
It currently has six executive and seven non-executive directors.
